title: Higher bounded monomials of a p-independent tuple remain independent over power subfields
statement: Let $p$ be prime and let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-field]. Let $r\geq0$ and $b_1,\ldots,b_r\in k$, and write $b^E=\prod_{i=1}^r b_i^{E_i}$. Suppose the family $(b^E)_{E\in\{0,\ldots,p-1\}^r}$ is linearly independent over $k^p=\{a^p:a\in k\}$. For every integer $n\geq0$, the family $(b^E)_{E\in\{0,\ldots,p^n-1\}^r}$ is linearly independent over the subfield $k^{p^n}=\{a^{p^n}:a\in k\}$. Explicitly, if coefficients $c_E\in k^{p^n}$ satisfy $\sum_E c_E b^E=0$, then every $c_E=0$. Empty products are $1$, so for $r=0$ the family is $(1)$; for $n=0$ it is also $(1)$, over $k$.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, proof p-base preparation paragraph; explicit higher-digit refinement of Tag 07P1, definition-p-basis, p-independent monomials.

proof.text: Induct on $n$, for the fixed tuple in the statement, using the explicit vanishing-of-coefficients criterion. At $n=0$ the only exponent vector is $0$, its monomial is $1$, and a relation $c_0\cdot1=0$ says $c_0=0$. This also treats the empty tuple for every $n$: there is exactly one empty exponent vector and its monomial is $1$.

source.place: Tag 07P1 (definition-p-basis), definition of p-independence; elementary higher-digit induction supplied by Q32 for the p-base preparation in Tag 09II (proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type).

proof.text: Assume the conclusion at $n$ and consider a relation $\sum_E c_Eb^E=0$ with $0\leq E_i<p^{n+1}$ and $c_E\in k^{p^{n+1}}$. Since $p>0$, coordinatewise Euclidean division gives a unique $E=A+pB$ with $0\leq A_i<p$ and $0\leq B_i<p^n$; conversely each such pair gives an allowed $E$. Write $c_{A+pB}=a_{A,B}^{p^{n+1}}$ with $a_{A,B}\in k$, and put $d_{A,B}=a_{A,B}^{p^n}\in k^{p^n}$. Then $c_{A+pB}=d_{A,B}^{p}$.

source.place: Tag 07P1 (definition-p-basis), definition of p-independence; elementary higher-digit induction supplied by Q32 for the p-base preparation in Tag 09II (proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type).

proof.text: For each $A$ put $S_A=\sum_B d_{A,B}b^B\in k$. By [def-weil-ring-frobenius], $x\mapsto x^p$ preserves finite sums and products. Thus $S_A^p=\sum_B d_{A,B}^p(b^B)^p$; reindexing the original finite sum by step 2 and using $b^{A+pB}=b^A(b^B)^p$ gives $0=\sum_A S_A^p b^A$. Each $S_A^p$ lies in $k^p$, so the assumed independence of the $p$-bounded monomials gives $S_A^p=0$ for every $A$.

source.place: Tag 03SM (definition-absolute-frobenius), following paragraph: the ring Frobenius is a ring endomorphism; elementary finite-sum expansion.

proof.text: A field has no nonzero element $z$ with $z^p=0$: if $z\neq0$, multiplication by $(z^{-1})^p$ would give $1=0$, contradicting [def-weil-field]. Hence every $S_A=0$. For each fixed $A$ this is a relation $\sum_B d_{A,B}b^B=0$ among the $p^n$-bounded monomials, with coefficients in $k^{p^n}$. The induction hypothesis gives every $d_{A,B}=0$, hence $c_{A+pB}=d_{A,B}^p=0$. The bijection of step 2 exhausts all $E$, completing the induction.
